english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the Great Four Limbs (Mahācatuṣpāda).

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus indeed spoke the venerable Ātreya.

hindi: भिषक् भेषज को चतुष्पाद और षोडशकल कहते हैं; जिसे पिछले अध्याय में षोडशगुण कहा गया है, वह भेषज युक्ति से युक्त होने पर आरोग्य के लिए समर्थ है — ऐसा भगवान् पुनर्वसु आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Physicians speak of medicine (bheṣaja) as having four limbs and sixteen parts; what was called "sixteen-qualitied" in the previous chapter, that medicine, applied with rational planning (yukti), is capable of health: so said the venerable Punarvasu Ātreya.

text_flags.why: The subject of bhāṣante must be "physicians" (bhiṣajaḥ, nom. pl.); bheṣajo (bheṣajaḥ, masc.) gives no sense beside the neuter bheṣajam. Probable typo.

notes: "said" is not in the Sanskrit: the sentence ends "iti bhagavān punarvasur ātreyaḥ" with no verb; the verb is supplied from iti. The unit is prose although typed as "verse".

hindi: "नहीं", मैत्रेय ने कहा। क्या कारण है? क्योंकि कुछ आतुर, जो उपकरणों से युक्त, परिचारकों से सम्पन्न और आत्मवान् हैं तथा कुशल भिषकों द्वारा चिकित्सित हैं, स्वस्थ होते हुए दिखाई देते हैं, और वैसे ही युक्त अन्य मरते हुए; इसलिए भेषज अकिंचित्कर है, जैसे गड्ढे में और सरोवर में डाला गया थोड़ा जल, या बहती हुई नदी में, या धूल के ढेर पर बिखेरी गई मुट्ठी भर धूल। वैसे ही अन्य, जो उपकरणों से रहित, परिचारकों से रहित और अनात्मवान् हैं तथा अकुशल भिषकों द्वारा चिकित्सित हैं, स्वस्थ होते हुए दिखाई देते हैं, और वैसे ही स्थित अन्य मरते हुए।
english: "No," said Maitreya. "What is the reason? For some patients are seen who are provided with equipment, provided with attendants and self-controlled, and attended by skilled physicians, recovering; and others, similarly endowed, dying. Therefore medicine is ineffective, just as a little water poured into a pit and into a lake, or into a flowing river, or a handful of dust scattered on a dust-heap. Likewise others are seen, without equipment, without attendants and not self-controlled, and attended by unskilled physicians, recovering; and others, similarly placed, dying."
notes: "said" is supplied from "iti maitreyaḥ" (no verb in the Sanskrit). tathāyuktāḥ "similarly endowed/placed" refers back to the condition just described in each case. The token "---" is a printed dash. Maitreya's argument continues in unit P1. The unit is prose although typed as "verse".

hindi: "मैत्रेय! यह मिथ्या सोचा जाता है", आत्रेय ने कहा। क्या कारण है? जो यह कहा गया कि जो आतुर इस षोडशगुण से युक्त भेषज से उपचार पाते हुए मरते हैं, वह उचित नहीं है; क्योंकि भेषज से साध्य व्याधियों में भेषज अकारण नहीं होता। और जो आतुर सम्पूर्ण भेषज के बिना स्वस्थ हो जाते हैं, ऐसा नहीं है कि सम्पूर्ण भेषज के उपपादन के लिए उनका समुत्थान-विशेष न हो; क्योंकि जैसे गिरे हुए, उठने में समर्थ पुरुष को उठाता हुआ पुरुष उसे बल दे, तो वह और शीघ्र, बिना क्लेश के उठ जाए, वैसे ही सम्पूर्ण भेषज की प्राप्ति से आतुर। और जो आतुर सम्पूर्ण भेषज से भी मरते हैं, वे सभी भेषज से युक्त होकर स्वस्थ नहीं हो जाते; क्योंकि सभी व्याधियाँ उपाय से साध्य नहीं होतीं, और उपाय से साध्य व्याधियों की बिना उपाय के सिद्धि नहीं होती, और असाध्य व्याधियों के लिए यह भेषज-समुदाय नहीं है; क्योंकि ज्ञानवान् भिषक् मरणासन्न आतुर को उठाने में समर्थ नहीं है। क्योंकि परीक्षा करके कार्य करने वाले कुशल होते हैं; जैसे योग को जानने वाला, नित्य अभ्यास करने वाला धनुर्धर धनुष लेकर, बहुत दूर न स्थित बड़े लक्ष्य पर बाण चलाता हुआ चूकता नहीं और इष्ट कार्य सिद्ध करता है, वैसे ही अपने गुणों से सम्पन्न, उपकरणों से युक्त भिषक् देखकर कर्म आरम्भ करता हुआ, बिना अपराध के, साध्य रोग वाले आतुर को अवश्य आरोग्य से युक्त कर देता है। इसलिए भेषज अभेषज से अभिन्न नहीं है।
english: "Maitreya, it is wrongly thought," said Ātreya. "What is the reason? What was said, that patients die though provided with this medicine endowed with sixteen qualities, is untenable; for in diseases curable by medicine, medicine is not a non-cause. And as for patients who recover without complete medicine, it is not that for them there is no special recovery for the provision of complete medicine; for just as a man raising a fallen man who is capable of rising might lend him his strength, and he would rise more quickly and without strain, so are patients through obtaining complete medicine. And as for patients who die even with complete medicine, not all of them, provided with medicine, would recover; for not all diseases are curable by means, nor is there success without the means for diseases curable by means, nor is this collection of medicine for incurable diseases; for a knowledgeable physician is not able to raise a patient who is about to die. For those who act after examination are the skilled; just as an archer who knows the technique (yoga) and is constant in practice, taking up the bow and shooting an arrow at a large target not too distant, does not miss, and accomplishes the desired task, so the physician endowed with his own qualities and equipped, having examined and beginning the action, without fault, surely endows the patient with a curable disease with health. Therefore medicine is not indistinguishable from non-medicine."

text_flags.why: "samaratham" is not a word here; samartham "capable" (of rising, utthānāya) fits the sense and the accusative with puruṣam. Probable typo.
The verb is sam-ud-√sthā (cf. samuttiṣṭhante, samuttiṣṭhamānāḥ in this chunk); "-tthiṣṭh-" is a misspelling of "-ttiṣṭh-". Probable typo.

notes: "said" is supplied from "iti ātreyaḥ". kevala is taken as "complete, whole" (it stands for the full sixteen-quality medicine named just before); the alternative sense "mere, alone" would make "kevalād bheṣajād ṛte" "without medicine alone". "na teṣāṃ ... samutthānaviśeṣo nāsti" is a double negative: it is not that they would have no better recovery; the dative "-upapādanāya" is rendered literally "for the provision of". "kāye" in the archer simile is taken as "body" in the sense of the target. "akāraṇam" = "not a cause". The unit is prose although typed as "verse".

hindi: और यह हमें प्रत्यक्ष है कि हम आतुर की अनातुर भेषज से चिकित्सा करते हैं, क्षाम की अक्षाम से; कृश और दुर्बल को हम पुष्ट करते हैं, स्थूल मेदस्वी का अपतर्पण करते हैं, उष्ण से अभिभूत का शीत से उपचार करते हैं, शीत से अभिभूत का उष्ण से; न्यून धातुओं को पूर्ण करते हैं, बढ़े हुओं को घटाते हैं; व्याधियों का मूल के विपर्यय से उपचार करते हुए उन्हें सम्यक् प्रकृति में स्थापित करते हैं। ऐसा करने वाले हम लोगों के लिए यह भेषज-समुदाय अत्यन्त प्रिय है।
english: And this is evident to us: that we treat the sick with medicine that is not sick, the wasted with the not-wasted; we nourish the lean and weak, we deplete the stout and fat, we treat one overcome by heat with cold, one overcome by cold with heat; we fill up deficient dhātus, we reduce those in excess; treating diseases by reversal of their root, we properly establish them in the natural state (prakṛti). For us who act thus, this collection of medicine is the most desirable.
notes: The object of "sthāpayāmaḥ" is not expressed; "them" follows vyādhīn grammatically, though the sense may be the patient or the dhātus. "anātureṇa bheṣajena" is literal ("with not-sick medicine"); the examples that follow are treatment by opposites. kāntatama, literally "most beloved/pleasing", rendered "most desirable". The token "pratyakṣaṃ---yadanātureṇa" has a printed dash inside it. The unit is prose although typed as "verse".

english: And here there are: the physician who knows the division of curable and incurable, guided by knowledge and at the right time, begins an action; that he certainly accomplishes.
notes: "bhavanti cātra" introduces the verses (the word "ślokāḥ" is not printed). "yat tat" = "which ... that" (the action he begins, that he accomplishes).

english: The physician who would treat the incurable would inevitably incur loss of wealth, learning and fame, censure, and non-acceptance.
notes: asaṃgraha, literally "non-gathering", is taken as "not being accepted (by people)"; it could also mean "failure to gain (patients or means)".

hindi: साध्य सुखसाध्य और कृच्छ्रसाध्य भी माना गया है; और असाध्य भी दो प्रकार का होता है — याप्य और जो अनुपक्रम है।
english: The curable is held to be easily curable and also curable with difficulty; and the incurable too is two-fold: the palliable (yāpya) and that which is untreatable (anupakrama).

hindi: और साध्यों का अल्प, मध्यम और उत्कृष्ट के अनुसार तीन प्रकार का विकल्प है; किन्तु नियत असाध्यों की विकल्पना नहीं होती।
english: And of the curable there is a three-fold gradation according to mild, moderate and severe; but of the incurable, which are fixed, there is no gradation.

hindi: जिसके हेतु, पूर्वरूप और रूप अल्प हों, और न दूष्य तुल्य गुण वाला हो, न दोष प्रकृति हो;
english: One whose causes, prodromal signs and symptoms are few, and whose dūṣya (what is vitiated) is not of similar quality, nor the doṣa the constitution (prakṛti);
notes: The sentence runs from unit 11 to unit 13 (marks of the easily curable). "tulyaguṇa" does not say similar to what; the doṣa is the natural reading, but it is not stated. "na doṣaḥ prakṛtir bhavet" is literal: "nor would the doṣa be the prakṛti", i.e. not the same doṣa as the constitution.

hindi: उत्पत्ति में एक दोष हो, देह सब औषधियों को सहने में समर्थ हो, और चतुष्पाद की उपपत्ति हो — यह सुखसाध्य का लक्षण है।
english: a single doṣa at the origin, a body able to bear all medicines, and the presence of the four limbs (catuṣpāda): the mark of the easily curable.

english: and diseases of four kinds of gradation, each with its own characteristics, on which treatment depends, are stated in the Mahācatuṣpāda.
notes: The four kinds are those of units 9 to 10 (easily curable, curable with difficulty, palliable, to be rejected).

hindi: अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र में, श्लोकस्थान में महाचतुष्पाद नामक दसवाँ अध्याय।
english: In the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Ślokasthāna, the tenth chapter named Mahācatuṣpāda.
notes: Chapter colophon.
